newsitem.title: INDIA: Cochin Refineries to start production soon.
newsitem.headline: Cochin Refineries to start production soon.

text.p: Indian state-controlled crude oil refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd said on Wednesday it expected to resume operations within the next two or three days.
"Hopefully the problem will be resolved in the next two to three days," company spokesman Sajeev Nair said by telephone from Cochin city in the southern state of Kerala.

Production at the 150,000 barrels-per-day refinery, located on the southwest coast of India, ground to a halt on Monday as the water supply dwindled to 8,450 kilolitres per day, compared to the refinery's daily demand of 22,750 kilolitres.
The refinery supplies petrol, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and diesel to the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Irrigation department officials said low electricity voltage and leaks in supply pipes, which were responsible for the sharp drop in water supply, had been fixed.

"There was a leakage in the pipeline which has been repaired now and the voltage has also been adjusted after a meeting with the electricity board," said Annamma (one name), a Kerala irrigation department official.
Nair said: "We will start production as soon as we are able to store water for at least three days. We cannot afford to have another shutdown."
The daily water supply to the refinery increased to nearly 20,000 kilolitres on Wednesday, Nair said.
He said the state government was making serious efforts to resolve the crisis because it was losing nearly 30 million rupees ($838,000) daily due to the shutdown.
Nair said the refinery had barely two days' stocks of diesel left but added that stocks of other products would last a week.
He said it would take the refinery nearly one week after it re-opened to reach its optimum capacity. The refinery's annual capacity is 7.5 million tonnes.
Nair said the refinery's crude shipments had not been affected but a backlog of crude shipments could mount if the problem persisted.
